approvedNativePactDirection.rationale: Tester reports converting Pacts to Invocations increases build variety but weakens Pact identity. Dedicated Pact entitlements preserve a distinct meaningful Pact pillar while Pact-dependent Invocations retain customization. User approves first Pact at Warlock 1, with Patron as source, Pact as arrangement, and Invocations as additional clauses. This is a conceptual model, not a mandatory literal contract. Follow-up owner direction: a Pact is a major agreement and Invocations are pact-bound clauses that cease to function if their Pact breaks, subject to explicit restoration or transfer terms of a newly made Pact. Preserve optional additional Pacts and defer gating. Reaffirmed: individual Pacts may restrict eligible Patrons; individual Invocations may restrict the Pact they are attached to, the Patron of that Pact, or both. Evaluate the specific Pact-Patron pairing, especially when additional Pacts or transfers are eventually possible. Owner clarifies that this architecture gives the Patron discretion over the terms and clauses they are willing to accept, distinct from the character meeting general rules prerequisites. Owner approves SRD52 Pact of the Blade core mechanics as the native baseline while retaining separate examination of 2014 weapon-storage ritual and other discrepancies. Owner finds unchanged base Pact underwhelming for a standalone pillar; do not treat bare SRD52 Pact as complete progression or preapprove any automatic extra attacks. Owner approves intrinsic Blade Pact second attack at Warlock level 5, consuming no Invocation, after observing that requiring Thirsting Blade as an Invocation creates an underwhelming Pact. BG3's Deepened Pact independently corroborates the proposed mechanical direction; other BG3 changes remain comparison candidates, not approved native grants. Owner approves BG3-style automatic level-5 improvements for all three Pact categories (Blade attack already settled, Chain familiar extra attack, Tome three free third-level spells) without spending Invocations. User also approves BG3 mundane-weapon binding for Blade; that weapon-specific effect does not apply to Chain or Tome. Hexblade patron-to-Pact classification remains under consideration; lore/source research only, no new playable parts. Owner extends Pact reconciliation from three to five, adding non-SRD official Talisman and unpublished UA Star Chain as comparative design cases; Star Chain's original Seeker-linked Patron prerequisite remains explicit and may only be broadened by later approved exception. Earlier editions' source-oriented Pact types map to Patrons instead of the Pact specialization pillar. Subsequent owner decision suspends both Seeker Patron and Star Chain Pact as an inseparable pair because source is UA with insufficient development; preserve five-Pact research but actively reconcile only Blade, Chain, Tome, and Talisman. Native future design must require the pair bidirectionally, without asserting this reverse condition was a literal rule in the original UA. Original Unearthed Arcana The Faithful explicitly offers Seeker the Star Chain INSTEAD OF an existing Pact Boon; Star Chain depends on Seeker but Seeker does not depend on Star Chain. Both are independently disabled for now by owner direction; no historical source is deleted. Owner approves native Talisman Pact consolidation of 2019 UA unlimited 1d4 checks with untrained skill and 2020 Tasha's charge-limited 1d4 correction after failed ability checks; the two Talisman bonuses cannot stack on the same roll. One transferable Talisman, a 1-hour replacement ceremony and no recharge on replacement; shared PB/Long Rest charges. Warlock level 5 gains automatic Shared Ward Reaction within 60 ft for 2d6+CHA reduction, spending one charge, without using an Invocation. Rebuke, Protection, Bond remain selectable Pact-attached Invocations, with distinct resource ledgers where published. Talisman rules are approved as design, not yet native runtime active.

additionalPactDesignDirection.note: Do not permanently prohibit additional Pacts; they represent significant new agreements and belong to future advanced rules. The native first Pact remains a dedicated level-1 choice. Leave the level, cost, eligibility, maximum and invocation transfer terms undecided.

pactInvocationLifecycle.pactDependenceVsPrerequisite: Every Invocation has Pact affiliation, even when it does not list an individual Pact type as its game-mechanical prerequisite.
pactInvocationLifecycle.preservePlayerChoice: Pact loss should have identifiable Invocation effects, but rules for refunded selections, replacement clauses and negotiated restoration remain undecided.
pactInvocationLifecycle.compatibilityRevalidation: A Pact-bound Invocation cannot be enabled under an incompatible Pact or Patron merely by restoration/transfer terms. Revalidate explicit Pact/Patron-specific prerequisites when affiliation changes; rules for explicit exceptions or conversion remain deferred. The receiving Patron must also accept the restored or transferred clause (or inherited/previously-established terms must cover it); this does not waive explicit restrictions.

compatibilityRules.note: Examples are eligibility fixtures only and do not create real Fiend-only or Pact-only Invocations. Actual restrictions are authored individually, not assigned by category globally.

patronTermsAndWillingness.note: The Patron decides which agreements and clauses it will grant or accept, subject to the underlying game's explicit eligibility requirements. Inherited or indirect relationships may already have established terms without fresh direct negotiation.

pactProgressionConcern.issue: The 2024 Blade entry gives weapon access, while essential martial attack growth at higher levels is gated by optional Invocations.
pactProgressionConcern.guidingDistinction: A Pact should deliver a meaningful self-sustaining specialization across class progression; Invocations should be optional specializations rather than unavoidable taxes to maintain baseline competence.
